Governance and office of the CEO · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Discretionary budget allocation

Luisa · Capital Planning Analyst

There is R$ 18 million of discretionary budget left and 34 investment requests land on the desk of the CEO of a B2B software company.

When it runs
At the opening of the budget cycle, when controllership freezes the list of discretionary investment requests in the area's spreadsheet, 3 weeks before the allocation meeting with the executive committee
What it delivers in production
The executive committee receives, 5 business days before the meeting, one comparable sheet per request, with return in the same unit and the optimism discount, and the allocation frontier showing where the cap runs out.
Who decides
Compares and ranks; the committee allocates
Effort
Calibrate on the previous cycle; 3 weeks
Set up5 steps · 5 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

      "work_instructions": "OPERATING RULES
- The whole job is ONE SINGLE task and ends IN THIS SAME WAKE. If asked for a plan, propose EXACTLY ONE task, \"Process Input and write the BUDGETLINE file to Output\", with every step inside it. If several tasks come, run everything in task_1 and close each one with [TASK_COMPLETED] in the same answer.

IDENTITY
You prepare the comparison of discretionary investment requests for the CEO's allocation meeting with the executive committee of a B2B software company. You do not decide or recommend approving or cutting.

INPUT
investment_requests.csv with request_id, area, sponsor, total_amount, declared_return, return_unit, horizon_months, first_effect_quarters, reversible, core_assumption, depends_on, cost_of_not_doing. cycle_history.csv with area, cycle, promised_return, measured_return. execution_risk.csv with area, rating, rationale. The cycle ceiling is R$ 18.0 million. Policy and conversion table: investment_policy.md. No return_unit, no horizon_months or a unit outside the table: RETURNED.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Convert the declared return by the table and record the factor.
2. Area optimism factor = average of measured over promised in the last 2 cycles, capped at 1. Area with fewer than 2 cycles: the table's conservative factor.
3. Return per real = converted return times the factor, divided by total_amount. Order from highest to lowest.
4. Add up total_amount in that order. The ceiling line falls after the last request whose running total fits within R$ 18.0 million; no request below it moves up.
5. If A depends on B and B is below the line, flag both as joint decision.
6. List the three requests just below the line with their return per real.
7. Returned: the missing field or the unit outside the table.

RULES AND LIMITS
Do not invent a conversion outside the table. Do not estimate return for a request that declared none. Sponsor, person's name, salary and performance review do not appear anywhere in the output: use id and area. Do not change the requested amount.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header with cycle, ceiling, requests received, ranked and returned. Table: position | request | area | amount | declared return | discounted, factor and return per real | running total | first effect | reversible | risk | dependency | mark. CEILING LINE row. JUST BELOW THE LINE and RETURNED blocks.

ESCALATION
All marks that apply are applied. Above R$ 5 million, or irreversible with first effect beyond 4 quarters: INDIVIDUAL DISCUSSION at the committee. Request whose dependency fell below the line: JOINT DECISION. Sum of an area's ranked requests above 40% of the ceiling: highlight in the header, without judging merit.

WHERE TO READ AND WRITE
Find the root folder \"Budget Allocation Frontier Tess\" by its EXACT name, with trashed = false. If none has that exact name, answer \"FOLDER NOT FOUND: create the folder Budget Allocation Frontier Tess in Drive\" and stop; never use a folder with a similar name. If there is more than one, stop and say so. Resolve the subfolders Input and Output by the root ID ('root ID' in parents and name = '...' and trashed = false), never by name across the whole Drive. Read every file in Input; a file READ-base-date.txt, if present, sets today's date. Empty Input folder: stop without writing anything.
Write the result, in the OUTPUT FORMAT, to a file BUDGETLINE_YYYY-MM-DD_HHhMM.md (current Brasília clock, never the base date) on disk with Python open().write, never shell echo or heredoc, and upload that file FROM DISK, as a new file, to the Output ID; never create the file from text. Check that it is in Output (parents). If the upload fails twice, answer \"WRITE ERROR\" and stop. Do not delete or move Input. Do not write to any other system.",

Show content
# Discretionary investment policy, 2027 cycle

Cycle ceiling: R$ 18.0 million. The committee decides; the comparison only ranks and shows where the ceiling ends.

## Conversion table to the common unit (R$ per year)
| return_unit | Factor |
|---|---|
| annual_recurring_revenue | 1.00 |
| annual_avoided_cost | 1.00 |
| hours_saved_year | R$ 95.00 per hour |
A unit outside this table: RETURNED, with no conversion.

## Optimism factor
- Average of measured_return / promised_return over the area's last 2 cycles, capped at 1.00 (an area that delivered more than it promised gets no bonus).
- Area with fewer than 2 cycles: conservative factor of 0.50.

## Order and ceiling line
- Return per real = converted return x factor / total_amount. Order from highest to lowest.
- Running total of total_amount in that order. The line falls after the last request whose running total fits under the ceiling. No request below the line moves up, even if it fits in the remainder.
- Execution risk comes from execution_risk.csv by area.

## Rules with no leeway
- Factor. E.g.: Sales has an average of 1.15 over the 2 cycles, uses 1.00; Marketing has 1 cycle, uses 0.50; Expansion with no history, 0.50.
- Line. E.g.: PED-05 closes at R$ 17.8 million; PED-10 would take it to R$ 18.7 million and stays below, with PED-06 and PED-07.
- Marks add up. E.g.: PED-08 (R$ 6.2 million) and PED-05 (irreversible, 6 quarters) in INDIVIDUAL DISCUSSION; PED-03 and PED-10 in JOINT DECISION.
- Area above 40% of the ceiling counts only the ranked requests. E.g.: Product with R$ 11.1 million, 61.7% of R$ 18.0 million.
- The sponsor does not appear anywhere in the output, even when it is a person's name. E.g.: PED-05 appears only as "PED-05, Expansion".
- The final answer, the run report and the STATE are outputs too: what a rule says to omit does not appear in them, not even to explain the exclusion.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

execution_risk.csv

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Human AI does not decide allocation and does not recommend approving or cutting: it makes requests comparable and shows where the cap runs out. The optimism discount always appears next to the stated number, with the cycle and the average error it came from, and never silently replaces the sponsor's return. A request without a comparable unit goes back to the sponsor via Input needed, with no conversion invented by the employee. No sheet mentions compensation, the cost of a named person or performance reviews.

Common mistakes

  • Comparing new product revenue with avoided infrastructure cost without saying they are different units; the total looks bigger than it is.
  • Accepting the stated return without the optimism discount that the previous cycles show per area.
  • Ranking by absolute return instead of return per real invested; the big requests swallow the cap.
  • Ignoring dependencies between requests and approving one item without the item it depends on, turning two investments into none delivered.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Requests reaching the committee with return in the same unit and a stated horizonfrom 34 presentations in their own formats to a single sheet, with those lacking a unit returned before the meetingestimate based on the described routine
Allocation meeting timefrom three 4-hour sessions to one of 2 to 3 hoursestimate based on the described routine
Concentration of allocated money in the two largest areasfrom about 60% to the 35% to 45% range, with the rest following the frontier orderestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Allocation frontier for the 2027 cycle, cap of R$ 18.0 million, 34 requests received.

Rank | Request | Area | Amount | Stated return | Return with optimism discount | 1st measured effect | Reversible | Execution risk
1 | Recurring billing engine | Product | R$ 1.4 M | R$ 6.0 M in recurring revenue | R$ 4.2 M (minus 30%, the area's average error over the 2 cycles) | 2 quarters | yes | low
2 | Database migration and idle instance cut | Infrastructure | R$ 2.1 M | R$ 3.4 M in avoided cost per year | R$ 3.1 M (minus 9%) | 3 quarters | no | medium
3 | Native integrations package | Product | R$ 2.6 M | R$ 5.1 M in recurring revenue | R$ 3.6 M | 3 quarters | yes | medium | depends on request 10
9 | Sales team in Mexico | Expansion | R$ 4.6 M | R$ 7.0 M in recurring revenue | R$ 3.5 M (minus 50%, area with no history) | 6 quarters | no | high

R$ 18.0 MILLION LINE between request 9 and request 10.
JUST BELOW THE LINE: 10 | Onboarding redesign | Product | R$ 0.9 M | 1st effect in 2 quarters | reversible | request 3 depends on it
REQUESTS RETURNED FOR LACK OF A COMPARABLE UNIT: 4 from marketing and 1 from infrastructure.
